title: Roof drain in a low-slope roof

checklist.item: The drain sits in a sump with tapered insulation, so the membrane slopes to it from all sides.
checklist.why: A drain at the high point of its own insulation ponds water around it.

checklist.item: The membrane is clamped in the drain's clamping ring, with a reinforced target sheet.
checklist.why: The clamp is the seal; an adhered edge alone peels.

checklist.item: A secondary (overflow) drain or scupper is shown, with its inlet 2 in (50 mm) above the low point, on separate piping.
checklist.why: Blocked primary drains collapse roofs; the overflow is a code requirement.

checklist.item: The drain body is fixed to the deck with an underdeck clamp, and an expansion joint is shown in the leader where needed.
checklist.why: A loose drain body tears the membrane as the roof moves.

checklist.item: Drain body and leader are insulated where they pass through conditioned space.
checklist.why: Cold leaders drip condensation onto ceilings.

checklist.item: Strainer dome, drain size and the plumbing reference are noted.
checklist.why: Drain size comes from the plumbing design, not the detail.
